title: Draft: render the proposed cad_sticker record
description: Adds functionality to render the proposed cad_sticker record, allowing for the display of stickers on 3D models with specified artwork and dimensions.
body:
Draft to show what the `cad_sticker` record (tscircuit/circuit-json#1018, for `<assembly.sticker />` in tscircuit/props#1026) looks like when rendered. Both of those are merged; this draft still carries its own copy of the record type until the installed circuit-json includes it.

The render is the new snapshot, `tests/features/assembly/__snapshots__/assembly-sticker1.snap.png`, viewable under Files changed.

## What it does

- `lib/converters/sticker.ts` turns a `cad_sticker` into a thin slab built from the record's world frame, with the artwork as a texture on the outward face. Artwork comes from `image_asset`; its `mimetype` decides whether it is rasterized from SVG over `background_color` or used as is.
- `convertCircuitJsonTo3D` picks the records up by their `type`, since the installed circuit-json does not know them yet.
- `tests/fixtures/nema17-enclosure-sticker.ts` recreates the USB stepper driver enclosure: the pinned NEMA17 and controller models, a JSCAD lid and screws, and the product label as a `cad_sticker`. The artwork is the production enclosure label from tscircuit/product-packaging (`products/nema17/enclosure-label/label.svg`), at its real 38.1 × 19.05 mm size.
- `assembly-sticker2.test.ts` checks where the artwork's corners land for a sticker on top, one turned a quarter turn, and one on a side wall.

## Not handled yet

- Explosions do not move a sticker with the part it is applied to.
- Transparent pixels in raster artwork are not composited over `background_color`.
- The pinned controller model is the older board revision, so one of the two USB-C openings shows the board rather than a connector.

Export `RegionalForceImproveSolver` so callers can reject a node's force improvement while preserving its original legal routes. On H616, the optimization moves a signal via too close to a DDR pad and causes an otherwise routable region to be discarded.

title: fix: center crystals between stacked load capacitors
description: Fixes crystal positioning issue when load capacitors are stacked above and below the crystal, ensuring the crystal is centered vertically between the capacitor bodies.
body: Stacked on #472. `CrystalNotCenteredOverLoadCapacitors` assumed load capacitors sit side by side, one under each crystal pin, and moved the crystal to the midpoint of their load-pin x positions. When the capacitors are stacked above and below the crystal, as in TI's TPS25751EVM (Figure 5-7), both load pins share one column. The midpoint is then that column, so a centered crystal was reported and told to move onto it. ### TI reference [TPS25751EVM user's guide (SLVUCP9B)](https://www.ti.com/lit/ug/slvucp9b/slvucp9b.pdf#page=44), Figure 5-7, page 44: Y1 between C41 (above) and C42 (below). The pin mapping differs from tscircuit's four-pin crystal symbol. TI's symbol has both crystal pins (1 and 3) on the right and both ground pins (2 and 4) on the left, while tscircuit's `crystal_4pin_right` puts X1 and X2 on opposite sides. The layout is still correct with our symbol: the capacitors are stacked above and below Y1, and Y1 is centered between them. ### Change When the two load pins share an x (within the existing 0.1 tolerance) and differ in y, the capacitors are treated as stacked: - the crystal should be vertically centered between the capacitor bodies; - horizontally it only needs to lie within the capacitors' extent, otherwise it's moved to the middle of it; - the message says "centered between C42 and C41" instead of mentioning load-pin alignment. Side-by-side layouts are unchanged. ### Tests - `ti-tps25751evm-stacked-crystal-caps`: the #472 repro now reports no crystal warning; test and snapshot updated. - `ti-tps25751evm-stacked-crystal-caps-off-center` (new): Y1 moved 1.2 toward C42 is still reported, with a move back to y = 7.9 and no x change. Validation: `bun test` (346 pass), `bun run typecheck`. Snapshots visually inspected. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: test: reproduce false crystal-centering warning for stacked load caps
description: Reproduces a false warning for crystal centering when load capacitors are stacked, ensuring the warning is correctly asserted in tests.
body:
TI's TPS25751EVM draws the 16 MHz crystal Y1 between its two load capacitors: C41 directly above and C42 directly below, both horizontal, with their ground ends on the left and their load ends in one column on the right. Y1 is centered between them (y = 7.896, halfway between 9.697 and 6.097) and within 0.2 of their horizontal centers.

`CrystalNotCenteredOverLoadCapacitors` assumes load caps sit side by side, one under each crystal pin. It averages the two load-pin x positions, which here are both 0.4, and reports Y1 as off-center, suggesting a move onto that shared column (`deltaSchX=+0.5`).

This adds a schematic-only TSX extract of Y1, C41, C42 and U7 (the oscillator host, with its supply and ground pins on net labels) and an SVG snapshot with the analysis below the schematic. Components and positions are copied unchanged from the transcription in tscircuit/checks#578. The test runs only `CrystalNotCenteredOverLoadCapacitors` and asserts the current incorrect Y1 warning. No solver changes are included; the fix is stacked in #473.

Reference: [TPS25751EVM user's guide (SLVUCP9B)](https://www.ti.com/lit/ug/slvucp9b/slvucp9b.pdf#page=44), Figure 5-7, page 44.

title: fix: let bootstrap capacitors and series supply resistors lie horizontally
description: Fixes orientation rules for bootstrap capacitors and series supply resistors to allow horizontal placement based on TI reference designs.
body:
Stacked on #475.

`TwoPinComponentShouldBeVertical` asked TI's bootstrap capacitor C64 and the series VPWR option R112 (TPS25751EVM) to stand vertically. TI reference schematics draw both kinds of part in either orientation, so neither is a supply-to-ground shunt.

### TI references
Bootstrap capacitors (BOOT/CBOOT to SW):

| EVM | Part | Orientation |
|---|---|---|
| [LM706A0-Q1 EVM (SNVU917)](https://www.ti.com/lit/ug/snvu917/snvu917.pdf#page=14), Fig 4-1 | C12 | horizontal |
| [LM70880-Q1 EVM (SNVU872A)](https://www.ti.com/lit/ug/snvu872a/snvu872a.pdf#page=12), Fig 4-1 | C12 | horizontal |
| [TPS56637 EVM (SLVUBE3B)](https://www.ti.com/lit/ug/slvube3b/slvube3b.pdf#page=8), Fig 6-1 | C4 | horizontal |
| [TPS56837 EVM (SLVUCE1A)](https://www.ti.com/lit/ug/slvuce1a/slvuce1a.pdf#page=10), Fig 6-1 | C4 | horizontal |
| [TPS65994 EVM (SLVUBM1C)](https://www.ti.com/lit/ug/slvubm1c/slvubm1c.pdf#page=21), Fig 9-3 | C14, C15 | horizontal |
| [TPS25762/72-Q1 EVM (SLVUC03)](https://www.ti.com/lit/ug/slvuc03/slvuc03.pdf#page=10), Fig 6-2 | C6, C7 | vertical |
| [TPS25751 EVM (SLVUCP9B)](https://www.ti.com/lit/ug/slvucp9b/slvucp9b.pdf#page=40), Fig 5-3 | C64 | horizontal |

Resistors between two supply nodes:

| EVM | Part | Orientation |
|---|---|---|
| [ADS704X EVM (SBAU382A)](https://www.ti.com/lit/ug/sbau382a/sbau382a.pdf#page=23), Fig 5-8 | R1, R6, R13 (0 Ω supply links) | horizontal |
| same | R11, R12, R21, R22 (0 Ω into ADC supply pins) | vertical |
| [TPS65994 EVM (SLVUBM1C)](https://www.ti.com/lit/ug/slvubm1c/slvubm1c.pdf#page=21), Fig 9-3 | R112 (0 Ω, jack → SYS_PWR); R29, R30 (2.2 Ω) | horizontal |
| [TPS25751 EVM (SLVUCP9B)](https://www.ti.com/lit/ug/slvucp9b/slvucp9b.pdf#page=42), Fig 5-5 | R112 | horizontal |
| same | R111 | vertical |

### Change
- **Bootstrap capacitors** (`isLocalFloatingChipCapacitor`): a capacitor from a chip's power-output pins to that same chip's `requiresPower` pin is exempt, and paralleled output pins of the host (U10's five SW pins) count as one node. A capacitor reaching another chip's supply, or two supply sources, is still checked.
- **Series resistors**: resistors join diodes, fuses and chips in the series power-path exemption when both ends are power nodes. A resistor from a supply to a signal pin is still checked.

### Test updates
- `ti-tps25751evm-horizontal-series-parts` (#475): C64 and R112 are no longer reported.
- `floating-chip-capacitor-orientation`: the fixture's "two-supplies" mode (output pin returning to the same chip's supply input) now joins the floating baseline with no warning; it is removed from `floating-chip-capacitor-rail-guards`, whose other guards are unchanged.
- New control `horizontal-supply-pull-up-control`: a horizontal 10 kΩ from V3V3 to an EN pin is still reported.
- Existing fixtures lose warnings on series resistors between two power-labeled nets; snapshots and counts updated:
  - esp32-usb-ducky: R19, R20, R21, R22 (0 Ω supply links)
  - allwinner-t113: R107, R108 (0 Ω buck → rail links), R_DBG_SENSE_H (22.1 kΩ)
  - rp2040 power input: R_PD_VSYS_FILTER (10 Ω), R_PD_SENSE_CHARGE (470 Ω)
  - branch-order: R_PD_VDD (1 kΩ into U_PD.VDD)

  R_DBG_SENSE_H and R_PD_SENSE_CHARGE feed sense nodes that are power-labeled by name; they follow the same rule as the other series parts.

Validation: `bun test` (346 pass), `bun run typecheck`. Snapshots visually inspected.

title: test: reproduce false vertical-orientation warnings on TI series parts
description: Reproduces false vertical-orientation warnings for two horizontal components in the TPS25751EVM schematic, specifically the bootstrap capacitor and a do-not-place resistor, without altering the solver.
body:
`TwoPinComponentShouldBeVertical` asks two horizontal parts in TI's TPS25751EVM to stand vertically, although neither is a shunt from a supply rail.

**C64 (Figure 5-3, page 40)** is the LM76005 bootstrap capacitor. TI draws it horizontally between U10.CBOOT and the SW/L7 node. The existing bootstrap exception (`isLocalFloatingChipCapacitor`) doesn't apply because the transcription marks CBOOT `requiresPower`, so both ends look like supplies, and because SW is five `providesPower` pins rather than one.

**R112 (Figure 5-5, page 42)** is a do-not-place 0 Ω option. TI draws it horizontally between the `TPD_VPWR` label and the U12.VPWR node that R111 feeds from LDO_3V3; the sheet note says to populate it for source-only use. Both ends are supply nodes, so R112 is a series element on the power path. The solver already lets diodes, fuses and chips between two power nets take either orientation, but not resistors.

This adds two schematic-only TSX extracts (U10 with L7 and C64; U12 with R111, R112 and C68) with SVG snapshots, the analysis below each schematic. Components, positions and pin attributes are copied unchanged from the transcription in tscircuit/checks#578; supply and ground pins leave on net labels. The test runs only `TwoPinComponentShouldBeVertical` and asserts the current incorrect warnings. R111, drawn vertically from LDO_3V3, is not reported. No solver changes are included; the fix will be stacked on this PR.

Reference: [TPS25751EVM user's guide (SLVUCP9B)](https://www.ti.com/lit/ug/slvucp9b/slvucp9b.pdf#page=40), figures 5-3 and 5-5.

Validation: the new test passes and `bun run typecheck` passes. Snapshots visually inspected.

title: fix: preserve complete braced model parameters
description: Fixes truncation of valid braced model parameters to their first token, ensuring complete parameter token spans are preserved for correct SPICE output.
body:
A valid braced model parameter was truncated to its first token, so switch compatibility rewriting could emit malformed SPICE. Preserve the complete parameter token span, including nested function calls, arithmetic, quote delimiters, and continuation whitespace. Stop at a whitespace-separated bare argument, so `.options reltol=0.001 interp` parses `reltol` as `0.001` without absorbing `interp`.

Stacked on the CI-passing snapshot repro #65. The repro test is unchanged; its snapshot now shows the complete parameters and valid serialized model.

This restacks @ugin-man's existing implementation from #12 and retains the original author commit. It provides the requested repro/fix stack; the implementation in #12 and this PR should not be merged independently.

Validation: all 108 parser tests and 14 snapshots pass; format, typecheck, and ESM/DTS build pass. Locally linked the parser into ngspice-spice-engine: its full 50-test suite passes, and real WASM simulations of raw and previously normalized expression-valued switches both complete with matching outputs.

Ten regression cases cover the reported bare-option boundary, multiple flags between assignments, scalar/quoted/braced/function/arithmetic expressions, and continuation lines. The new boundary cases failed before the correction. Default source serialization preserves the original card.

The published parser dependency must pick up this correction after release. This does not claim to resolve the independent full TI power-tree convergence failure.

title: Skip distant obstacles before scanning fanout aliases
description: Moves the existing distance check ahead of alias scans in fanout clearance checks, significantly reducing CPU time and improving search efficiency.
body:
Move the existing distance check ahead of alias scans in fanout clearance checks. Nearby obstacles keep every existing exemption. These scans accounted for 23.2% of sampled CPU time in the latest native profile.

Stacked on repro #293. The focused replay reads **99.6% fewer alias entries**. Matched native searches take **34.4% less time on iCE/Pi** and **36.7% less on i.MX6**, with identical copper.

| Measurement | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| iCE/Pi native search median | 176.5 s | 115.8 s (−34.4%) |
| i.MX6 native search median | 197.1 s | 124.8 s (−36.7%) |
| Focused replay: alias entries read | 33,498 | 132 (−99.6%) |
| Native search vias, each board | 7 | 7 |
| Native copper DRC issues | 0 | 0 |
| Fanout31 solved / timed out | 30 / 42 | 30 / 42 |
| Full boards completed | 0 / 6 | 0 / 6 |

Each native timing uses three serial matched pairs on one Blacksmith worker, alternating order. iCE/Pi still reaches only 7/32 fanouts; i.MX6 reaches 8/32. Their input and copper hashes match across versions.

All six boards were rerouted from empty copper with the normal fanout → DDR buses → remaining routing sequence. **All still stop in fanout; no DDR bus phase starts.** The separate-worker full i.MX6 run was slower (418 → 498 s); that observation remains in the analysis. The matched measurements above isolate native fanout search.

Adds `circuit-json-to-connectivity-map` 0.0.35 as a direct dependency and uses it for source-net membership. Adds helpers for source connection groups and two-terminal passive bridges so channel topology can follow series components.

`PassiveBridge` names the two source port IDs of a series component. `SourceConnectionGroup` names the source port and net IDs connected by a trace or by internal component wiring. `SourcePortId` and `SourceNetId` are shared aliases derived from the corresponding Circuit JSON records.

### New concepts

- **Source connectivity map.** It groups source ports and nets by electrical connection, including pins that a part marks as internally connected, such as USB shields or ESD pass-through pins.
- **Passive bridge.** A resistor, capacitor, or inductor with exactly two ports can bridge their nets for signal analysis when both ports are off the power and ground rails.

title: Render wire harness drawings
description: Renders wire harness (cable manufacturing) sheets from the elements proposed in tscircuitcircuit-json1023. TSX spec: tscircuitprops1030.
body:
Renders wire harness (cable manufacturing) sheets from the elements proposed in tscircuit/circuit-json#1023. TSX spec: tscircuit/props#1030.

[Motor cable harness sheet](`` https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-to-drawing/bcbf96ec60cd235e5c82949deb3d440e49871454/tests/__snapshots__/harness-drawing.snap.svg ``)

## What it draws

- `drawing_wiring_harness_view`: one `cad_cable` flattened, from end at left and to end at right. Connector outlines come from cableprinter body dimensions, with one ribbon per `cad_cable_wire`. Designators, pin numbers and the `nominal_length` dimension are derived from the cable.
- `drawing_table` / `drawing_table_cell`: a generic table placed by `anchor_position` and `anchor_alignment`, with merged cells and resolved text.
- `drawing_balloon`: circled callouts placed by their anchor; only the leader tip is resolved onto the connector or the wire bundle.

A page with only harness views or tables needs no `resolveScene`.

## Crossed wires

Wires run in evenly spaced lanes and change lanes only in the middle of the cable. Two wires cross exactly once when their order differs between the ends and never otherwise, no crossing sits on a bend or on another crossing, and the wire passing over is drawn unbroken with a small gap in the one beneath. `tests/harness-crossings.test.ts` checks this for every wiring of up to six wires (873 layouts) and for pin-for-pin cables up to 16 pins. Wirings with no layout of one straight run per wire fall back to exchanging neighbouring wires step by step.

## Notes for review

- **Vector, not PoppyGL.** AGENTS.md says drawing views always use PoppyGL outline rendering. Harness views are drawn as vectors instead: the cable length is not to scale and the crossings are schematic, so there is no real geometry to outline. If this is accepted, that rule needs a harness exception.
- **circuit-json.** Requires `circuit-json` 0.0.556, which includes the elements from tscircuit/circuit-json#1023.
- **New dependency.** `@tscircuit/cableprinter` supplies connector dimensions. Adapter cable ends are parsed separately because cableprinter rejects adapters whose ends differ in contact count, such as `adaptercable_a(jst_ph_pins6)_b(jst_ph_pins4)`.
- **Layout convention.** The cable is drawn lying flat, so from-end pin 1 is at the top and to-end pin 1 at the bottom, and a pin-for-pin cable is drawn fully crossed.
- A `$` in authored text is now kept literal when page content is inserted into the SVG.
- No README changes.

title: Add pill-shaped solder paste props
description: Adds support for pill-shaped solder paste props to the existing API, allowing for the representation of oval and rotated paste-only apertures in PCB designs.
body:
Jan Mrázek's November 9 feedback, item 26, identifies missing support for oval and rotated paste-only apertures. These openings define the solder stencil independently of copper pads. The existing solder-paste props accept only circles and rectangles, so Core cannot represent imported pill apertures through the ordinary SolderPaste component.

Add pill-shaped solder paste to the existing props API, reusing the shared pill dimensions and normal PCB placement, including pcbRotation. An explicit radius preserves both capsules and rounded rectangles. Dimensions and radius accept numbers in mm or distance strings; parsed values are numbers. Required generated API references are included.

title: Resolve relative model paths in tsci export glb and gltf (#5654)
description: Fixes 404 errors when exporting glb and gltf formats by ensuring relative model paths are converted to file URLs before processing.
body:
**Stack:** 2/2, #5875, the repro → this fix. Merge this into the repro branch first, then merge #5875 to `main`.

Fixes #5654.

## Cause

`tsci build --glbs` passes Circuit JSON through `convertModelUrlsToFileUrls` before calling `convertCircuitJsonToGltf`. That turns a relative model path like `./libraries/cap.step` into a `file://` URL the converter can `fetch()`.

`tsci export` (`lib/shared/export-snippet.ts`) skipped that step for the `glb` and `gltf` formats. The converter received the bare relative path, and the fetch failed with `404 Not Found`.

## Change

The `glb` and `gltf` export branches now call `convertModelUrlsToFileUrls(circuitJson)` too, using the same helper `build-glbs.ts`, `render-drawing-pages.ts` and `render-explosion-video.ts` already import.

## Result

The repro test is unchanged. Its snapshot of `Failed to load STEP from …` messages goes from one entry to `[]`.

Checked by hand with `bun cli/main.ts export` on the repro's project:

| Command | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `tsci export -f glb` | 404, 21,772-byte GLB without the model | No error, 214,124 bytes, the same as `tsci build --glbs` |
| `tsci export -f gltf` | 404 | No error, model loaded |

The CLI test fixture can't run in my container, which has no IPv6 listen, so CI runs the test.

title: repro: Pipeline 9 routes bus wires on forbidden layers
description: Fixes autorouting failure by ensuring that Pipeline 9 respects layer restrictions for bus connections, preventing routing on forbidden layers.
body:
## Motivation

While routing our [fire-stick board](https://tscircuit.com/gokul/fire-stick), we restricted the C38-to-TP5 connection to the top and bottom layers. Pipeline 9 still reported success with wire segments on `inner1` and `inner2`.

The router should respect the requested layers, or report that it cannot complete a compliant route. Silently using forbidden layers makes the result unsuitable for the requested board layout.

## How it happens

The captured input includes a bus whose `allowedLayers` is `["top", "bottom"]`, and its connection name matches the routed connection. Pipeline 9 does not pass that bus restriction into path planning, so the route can use the board's inner layers.

## Reproduction

- Uses the unchanged four-layer routing input captured from our board; source and checksum are recorded alongside the compressed fixture.
- Checks actual nonzero wire segments on forbidden layers, not a through-via passing through those layers.
- Uses `test.failing` for the layer-compliance assertion. Solver completion and snapshot checks run separately in `beforeAll`, so unrelated failures are not hidden.
- Test-only: no production changes or board edits.

The snapshot shows component pads and the newly routed connection. Fixed-copper obstacles are hidden only in the picture; routing and DRC still use the complete input. The header distinguishes **zero relaxed DRC errors** from the forbidden inner-layer wires.

![Captured board routing](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GokulPandi-M/tscircuit-autorouter/7779ecccb7906568f4235f0d98981201087cb69c/tests/repro/__snapshots__/pipeline9-fire-stick-allowed-layers.snap.svg)

## Validation

- Reproduced against main `2b1207a` (0.0.1135).
- Targeted test and snapshot passed with the expected-failure marker.
- Removing the marker fails specifically on `inner1` and `inner2` wire segments.
- Snapshot visually inspected.
- Updated snapshot regenerated, visually inspected, and verified by the targeted test. CI is pending for this update.

title: Place shared ground labels at the lower end of their rail
description: Fixes the placement of shared ground labels on the power-stage sheet to ensure they are positioned at the lower end of their respective rails instead of hanging from stubs.
body:
Stacked on tscircuit/schematic-trace-solver#1450 (the TPS25751EVM power-stage repro).

## Problem
On the power-stage sheet, U10 ties its pins into two ground rails, but neither GND symbol sits at the end of its rail:
- **Left rail (NC pins, PGOOD, SYNC_MODE):** the symbol hangs from a stub that leaves pin 30 and crosses the rail to the left, instead of hanging straight down from the rail's lower end.
- **Right rail (BIAS, AGND, PGND, PAD):** the symbol hangs from a stub off the BIAS pin at the top of the rail, instead of from the rail's lower end at PAD (pin 31).

## Cause
**Left rail.** `AvailableNetOrientationSolver` already finds the rail's lower end as its host-rail candidate, and that candidate is clear. `canPlaceVerticalLabelOnHostRail` then rejects it for two reasons:
- It only accepts an end on the label's original trace pair (PGOOD–SYNC_MODE). The lower end is on another pairwise trace of the same continuous rail, which `getTraceAnchorCandidates` walks on purpose.
- It counts every pin of the component as covered by the label. PAD sits on the opposite side of U10, so a label beside the left side can't cover it.

**Right rail.** `Example28Solver` moves the BIAS trace outward to clear the U10_FB label, while the AGND/PGND/PAD chain stays in the inner column until `SameNetJunctionAlignmentSolver` aligns it. So when the GND label gets its orientation, the rail's lower end doesn't exist yet. The label is rotated in place on a connector stub off the BIAS pin stub. `placeGroundRailLabelsAtOuterEnd` follows only the column the label itself sits on, so it can't move a label hung from a stub.

## Fix
- **`AvailableNetOrientationSolver.canPlaceVerticalLabelOnHostRail`:** accepts an end on any trace of the continuous rail (`getTraceAnchorCandidates` now returns the `railTraceIds` it walks). It only checks pins on the rail's side of the component.
- **`placeGroundRailLabelsAtOuterEnd` (existing):** when a shared ground label hangs from its own connector stub, the function now follows the column of the rail the stub branches from, alongside the label's own column. It moves the label to whichever column reaches lowest.
  - Only stubs that the existing `getRemovableRailLabelConnectors` check says can be removed qualify, so no pin, branch or other label is stranded.
  - The existing clearance check still applies.
  - Its behavior without connector IDs is unchanged, so the `TraceCleanupSolver` caller isn't affected.
- **`SameNetJunctionAlignmentSolver`:** passes its connector IDs in, and drops a stub once its label has moved onto the rail.

No new files or helpers.

## Tests
- The power-stage repro now asserts that each U10 GND label faces down, sits on its rail, is at the rail's lowest point, and isn't on a connector stub. These assertions fail without the fix.
- Snapshot updates:
  - `repro-ti-tps25751evm-power-stage`: both GND symbols at their rail ends.
  - `esp8684-disconnected-power-label`: the V3V3_RF power label on VDDA3P31/32 now sits on its rail corner, and its outward connector stub is gone. Same cause as the left rail.
- `bun test`: 765 pass, 0 fail. `tsc --noEmit` and `biome format` are clean.

title: Preserve declared KiCad paste apertures and capsule geometry
description: Preserves declared KiCad paste apertures and capsule geometry for the USB1046 connector during import, ensuring accurate stencil geometry and pad representation.
body:
KiCad declares six top-side paste apertures for the unchanged USB1046 connector, but the importer drops them. Preserve those declared apertures independently of copper: paste-only pads produce stencil geometry, and copper pads retain links to their corresponding apertures.

KiCad's `oval` is a capsule, so it maps directly to Circuit JSON `pill`/`rotated_pill`; rounded rectangles retain their corner radius. No ellipse sampling or polygon approximation is involved. The helper also handles declared circle and rectangle apertures, paste layers, and KiCad pad/footprint paste margins using existing Circuit JSON shapes.

Conversion follows the library's existing patterns: `createSmdPad` returns its inserted pad ID directly, like `createPcbPort`, rather than discovering it by counting database rows. Copper and paste share a pure `getPadShape` helper for rectangle/capsule rotation, and paste uses the existing layer mapper. `processPad` emits paste once per source pad. Paste remains independent of copper because a paste-only opening has no copper pad to copy.

Stacked on the one-footprint repro: #325. This fix enables that same test and updates its visual snapshot from an empty converted stencil to the six openings shown by native KiCad. Source and test logic are otherwise unchanged.

Companion Core repro: https://github.com/tscircuit/core/pull/5723. Companion Core fix: https://github.com/tscircuit/core/pull/5724. Both stages are required: this producer emits the apertures; Core must preserve them when rebuilding the footprint.

Validation:
- The native-KiCad comparison and six-aperture assertion pass; the repro and eight neighboring footprint tests also pass locally.
- 43 relevant local tests pass after simplification. Comparing 80 fixture/rotation conversions with the previous implementation yields identical output records, warnings and statistics.

title: fix: only align diode-resistor pairs joined by a private series node
description: Fixes alignment checks for diode-resistor pairs to only consider true series links, excluding shared rails and parallel pairs.
body: Stacked on #485. `DiodeResistorNotAligned` finds pairs two ways. The label-based check already skips shared rails ("a shared rail or fanout is not a series pair"). The trace-based check paired any diode and resistor joined by a drawn wire, so it asked rail-sharing and parallel pairs to line up end to end. ### Change A trace-based pair is now checked only when it's a real series link: - the node the wire joins is not a rail (same rule as the label-based check); - the two parts don't also share their other net (a parallel pair). Parallel pairs are already covered by `ParallelDiodeResistorNotAligned`, which still reports crossed branches. ### Effect - #485 repro: D3/R13 (shares only `730_LDO_3V3`) and D10/R85 (parallel between `TIVA_P3V3` and `T_RST`) are no longer reported. TI draws D10 and R85 side by side, as parallel parts should be ([Figure 5-7](https://www.ti.com/lit/ug/slvucp9b/slvucp9b.pdf#page=44)). - Existing fixtures lose the same kinds of pairing; snapshots and counts updated: - Allwinner T113: D_FEL_OR / R_USB0_BASE, which only share the `USB0_VBUS` rail. - QRNG dual amplifier: D_ZENER / R2E, which only share GND (17 issues, was 18). - RP2040 logic power: two D7 / R141 warnings. They're parallel between `POWER_ON_LEVEL` and GND; their crossed branches are still reported once by `ParallelDiodeResistorNotAligned` (5 issues, was 7; correction sheet 4, was 6). - New control `series-led-resistor-control`: an LED and its series resistor joined by a bent wire on a private node is still reported. Validation: `bun test --timeout 120000` (350 pass; the Allwinner snapshot test exceeds the default 5 s timeout locally), `bun run typecheck`. Snapshots visually inspected. ### Layout comparison Four layouts of each subcircuit, analyzed with the analyzer on `main` (old) and with this PR (new), to check that the warnings removed here are false positives. **D3 / R13** ([TI Figure 5-1, page 39](https://www.ti.com/lit/ug/slvucp9b/slvucp9b.pdf#page=39)): TI keeps D3's column beside U1 and gives D3 its own `730_LDO_3V3` label; the R13–R18 bus has a separate one. Top-left A, top-right B, bottom-left C, bottom-right D: | | Layout | Old | New | |---|---|---|---| | A | TI placement: D3/R19/Q1 beside U1 | D3/R13 flagged | – | | B | A with a shorter `schMaxTraceDistance` (router draws the same wire) | flagged | – | | C | D3 column moved beside the pull-up bank | – | – | | D | The warning's advice: D3 under R13 | – | – | C and D look tidier but don't work: Q1's gate (with R21) goes to U1 pin 6 (CAP_MIS) on U1's left side, so moving the column away from U1 sends that wire back under U1. A's placement is correct and matches TI, so the D3/R13 alignment warning is a false positive. A still has a long bent wire from D3's anode to the bus. That wire comes from the schematic router joining same-net parts, not from placement; TI avoids it with a local rail label. It belongs in a routing check, not `DiodeResistorNotAligned`. **D10 / R85** ([TI Figure 5-7, page 44](https://www.ti.com/lit/ug/slvucp9b/slvucp9b.pdf#page=44)): R85 and D10 side by side between TIVA_P3V3 and T_RST, D10 cathode up. | | Layout | Old | New | |---|---|---|---| | A | TI ladder, D10 corrected | D10/R85 flagged | – | | B | Reference schematic's reversed D10 | flagged | – | | C | The warning's advice: D10 on R85's axis (wire wraps around R85) | 3 warnings | `ParallelDiodeResistorNotAligned` (staggered) | | D | Parts squeezed together | overlap + flagged | overlap | A is the clearest layout and was flagged; following the advice (C) is worse. After this PR, C is still reported, by the parallel-pair check that fits it. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: test: reproduce diode-resistor alignment on rail-sharing and parallel pairs
description: Adds tests to reproduce and validate the alignment behavior of diode-resistor pairs in schematic analysis, specifically addressing incorrect warnings for series and parallel configurations.
body:
`DiodeResistorNotAligned` has two ways of finding a diode–resistor pair. The label-based check skips shared rails ("a shared rail or fanout is not a series pair"). The trace-based check pairs any diode and resistor joined by a drawn wire, so it also reports two TI TPS25751EVM pairs that aren't in series:

- **D3 / R13** ([Figure 5-1, page 39](https://www.ti.com/lit/ug/slvucp9b/slvucp9b.pdf#page=39)): D3's anode and R13 only share the `730_LDO_3V3` rail. D3's series resistor is R19, drawn below it.
- **D10 / R85** ([Figure 5-7, page 44](https://www.ti.com/lit/ug/slvucp9b/slvucp9b.pdf#page=44)): both connect `TIVA_P3V3` and `T_RST`, so they're in parallel. TI draws them side by side, which is correct for parallel parts.

Each is told to "align on the same axis and rotate" end to end.

This adds two schematic-only TSX extracts with SVG snapshots, the analysis below each schematic:
- D3, R19, Q1, R21 and the R13–R18 pull-up bank on the same rail; U1 pins leave on net labels.
- The TIVA reset network: R85, D10, S3 and C36.

Components and positions are copied from the reference schematic in tscircuit/checks, with **one correction to match TI**: D10 is connected cathode → `TIVA_P3V3` and anode → `T_RST`, triangle pointing up. The reference schematic currently has D10 reversed. The warning appears with either D10 orientation. The reset extract uses `schMaxTraceDistance={10}` so the router draws wires between the parts as it does on the full sheet.

The test runs only `DiodeResistorNotAligned` and asserts the current incorrect warnings. No solver changes are included; the fix will be stacked on this PR.

title: fix: allow one drawn pin pitch of padding in pin-padding solver
description: Fixes pin padding calculations to allow one drawn pitch of padding in the pin-padding solver, improving layout accuracy for components with varying pin spacing.
body: Stacked on #469. `SchematicPinPaddingToEdgeSolver` measured box padding against the component's nominal `pin_spacing`. When `schPinStyle` margins draw pin rows farther apart (0.4 or 0.8 instead of 0.2), a box with one drawn pitch of padding (the tightest uniform layout) was reported. The suggested resize also asked for less padding than one pitch. ### Change - The smallest drawn gap between adjacent pins on any side is now a floor for the allowed padding. The rest of the threshold, including the label-based allowance and the extra-pitch slack, is unchanged. - Gap comparisons use a 0.01 tolerance instead of `1e-9`, so fractional sizes copied from reference drawings (`schHeight={2.00106}`) don't trip the check. ### Effect - The #469 repro (J2, J3, J4, J5, J6, J7, J11, U5 from the TI TPS25751EVM) no longer reports pin padding; the test and snapshot are updated. The legitimate `GenericSchematicBoxTooWide` warnings on J2, J3, J4, J5 and U5 are still reported and asserted. - On the full seven-sheet TPS25751EVM board from tscircuit/checks#578, U1, U4, U7, U8 and U11 are still reported. U6 is no longer reported: its two right-side pins are drawn 0.8 apart with 0.8 padding. - `bldc-pin-padding-label-collisions-repro-U8` snapshot: U8 is still reported. Its suggested height grows slightly, because the suggestion now keeps one drawn pitch (0.6) of padding. Validation: `bun test` (345 pass), `bun run typecheck`. Snapshots visually inspected. ### Layout comparison J5 drawn four ways on one board at the same scale, analyzed with the analyzer on `main` (old) and with this PR (new). TI ([Figure 5-2, page 40](https://www.ti.com/lit/ug/slvucp9b/slvucp9b.pdf#page=40)) draws J5 with wide pin spacing and one pin gap from the outer pins to the box edges: Left to right A, B, C, D: | | Layout | Old padding | New padding | |---|---|---|---| | A | TI: 0.8 pin pitch, 0.8 edge padding | flagged (suggests B) | – | | B | The old suggested height: 0.2 padding | – | – | | C | Really over-padded: 1.8 padding | flagged | flagged | | D | Standard 0.2 pitch, compact box | – | – | D is the most compact J5, but what improves it is the smaller pin pitch, not the padding. The old warning pushed A toward B, where the outer pins hug the box edges. After this PR, A and B pass and the over-padded C is still caught. (`GenericSchematicBoxTooWide` is reported for all four, unchanged.) Flagging an over-wide pin pitch would be a separate check. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: test: reproduce false pin-padding warnings on TI TPS25751EVM boxes
description: Reproduces false SchematicPinPaddingToEdgeTooLarge warnings for eight boxes in the TI TPS25751EVM schematic due to incorrect pin padding calculations without altering the solver.
body:
Eight boxes from the TI TPS25751EVM transcription in tscircuit/checks#578 get a false `SchematicPinPaddingToEdgeTooLarge` warning: J2, J3, J4, J5, J6, J7, J11 and U5.

These boxes space their pin rows with `schPinStyle` margins, so the pins are drawn 0.4 apart (0.8 for J5 and U5), while the component's `pin_spacing` stays 0.2. Each box has about one drawn pin pitch between its outer pins and the box edge, which is the normal layout. The solver compares that padding against the nominal 0.2 spacing (allowing 0.2 + 0.2 = 0.4). Padding of 0.4005 from TI's fractional box heights then fails the `1e-9` comparison. Following the suggested heights would make the layout worse: J7 is told to shrink to `schHeight=1.601`, which leaves 0.2 of padding on a 0.4 pitch.

This adds a schematic-only TSX extract and an SVG snapshot with the analysis below the schematic. Box sizes, pin arrangements and pin styles are copied unchanged from the checks fixture; only positions are moved into a grid. The test captures the current incorrect behavior (eight warnings). No solver changes are included; the fix will be stacked on this PR.

Reference: [TPS25751EVM user's guide (SLVUCP9B)](https://www.ti.com/lit/ug/slvucp9b/slvucp9b.pdf), figures 5-2, 5-4 and 5-7.

title: fix: let 0 ohm links away from ground lie in line
description: Fixes the orientation check for 0 ohm links, allowing them to be drawn in line when not connected to ground, aligning with TIs reference designs.
body:
Stacked on #483.

`TwoPinComponentShouldBeVertical` told TI's 0 Ω rename link R68 (TPS25751EVM) to stand vertically, because its GPIO3 end shares the `TPD_VPWR` power net. #52 deliberately applied the rule to every resistor, including 0 Ω links. TI's reference schematics show the orientation of a 0 Ω part depends on whether it reaches ground.

### TI references
0 Ω links between a supply and another node are drawn in either orientation, following the layout:

| EVM | Part | Orientation |
|---|---|---|
| [TPS25751 EVM (SLVUCP9B)](https://www.ti.com/lit/ug/slvucp9b/slvucp9b.pdf#page=41), Fig 5-4 | R60, R61, R65, R68, R69, R70 (GPIO rename), R43 (GPIO3 → TPD_VPWR) | horizontal |
| [TPS25751 EVM](https://www.ti.com/lit/ug/slvucp9b/slvucp9b.pdf#page=42), Fig 5-5 | R112 (TPD_VPWR → VPWR) / R111 (LDO_3V3 → VPWR) | horizontal / vertical |
| [ADS704X EVM (SBAU382A)](https://www.ti.com/lit/ug/sbau382a/sbau382a.pdf#page=23), Fig 5-8 | R1, R6, R13 / R11, R12, R21, R22 | horizontal / vertical |
| [TPS65994 EVM (SLVUBM1C)](https://www.ti.com/lit/ug/slvubm1c/slvubm1c.pdf#page=21), Fig 9-3 | R112 (jack → SYS_PWR) | horizontal |
| [TPS25762/72-Q1 EVM (SLVUC03)](https://www.ti.com/lit/ug/slvuc03/slvuc03.pdf#page=10), Fig 6-2 | R10 (CSN/BUS path) | horizontal |

0 Ω straps to ground are drawn vertically:

| EVM | Part |
|---|---|
| [LM706A0-Q1 EVM (SNVU917)](https://www.ti.com/lit/ug/snvu917/snvu917.pdf#page=14), Fig 4-1 | R10 (BIAS → GND) |
| [TPS56637 EVM (SLVUBE3B)](https://www.ti.com/lit/ug/slvube3b/slvube3b.pdf#page=8), Fig 6-1 | R3 (MODE → AGND) |
| [ADS704X EVM (SBAU382A)](https://www.ti.com/lit/ug/sbau382a/sbau382a.pdf#page=23), Fig 5-8 | R4, R40, R43, R44 (→ AGND) |

### Change
The rail-orientation check skips a resistor whose `resistance` is 0 when neither end is a ground net. A 0 Ω strap to ground, and every non-zero resistor, are checked as before.

### Test updates
- `ti-tps25751evm-zero-ohm-name-change` (#483): R68 is no longer reported.
- `rail-connected-two-pin-orientation` (#52): R0, a 0 Ω link from VCC to a signal, is no longer reported (6 → 5 issues); the other five parts are unchanged. This reverses #52's choice for 0 Ω links that don't reach ground, based on the references above.
- New control `zero-ohm-ground-strap-control`: a horizontal 0 Ω strap from a pin to GND is still reported. The published `rcr-junction` fixture's 0 Ω strap R11 is also still reported.

Validation: `bun test` (350 pass), `bun run typecheck`. Snapshots visually inspected.

title: test: reproduce vertical-orientation warning on a TI 0 ohm rename link
description: Reproduces a warning for the vertical orientation of a 0 ohm link in the TI TPS25751EVM schematic.
body:
TI's TPS25751EVM renames six TPS25751 GPIO nets for the expansion header through 0 Ω links drawn horizontally in a row: R60, R61, R65, R68, R69 and R70 ("Zero Ohm Name Change", [Figure 5-4, page 41](https://www.ti.com/lit/ug/slvucp9b/slvucp9b.pdf#page=41)).

`TwoPinComponentShouldBeVertical` reports only R68. Its GPIO3 end shares a net with `TPD_VPWR`, which is marked as power (on the full board the TPS25751 GPIO3 output can power the TPD4S201 through R112). Its other end, A_GPIO3, is a plain signal, so R68 is read as a pull-up from a supply and told to stand vertically. R68 is a 0 Ω jumper that only renames the net; it isn't a shunt, and TI draws it in line with the other five links.

This adds a schematic-only TSX extract of the six links with an SVG snapshot, the analysis below the schematic. Components and positions are copied unchanged from the reference schematic in tscircuit/checks (merged from tscircuit/checks#578); GPIO3 is joined to `TPD_VPWR` and the nets are declared as in the reference board, so R68's pin 1 is drawn as a `TPD_VPWR` power symbol, as on the full board. The test runs only `TwoPinComponentShouldBeVertical` and asserts the current incorrect warning. No solver changes are included; the fix will be stacked on this PR.

title: feat: estimate IBIS output edge duration for channel endpoints
description: Adds edgeDurationSeconds to estimate the 1090 edge duration for channel endpoints, enabling accurate transient timestep sizing across fixtures.
body:
Adds `edgeDurationSeconds` so later channel stages can size the transient timestep and routed line cells. Stacked on #118. Requesting an output edge duration for an input-only pin raises a coded diagnostic.

### New concepts

- **10–90% edge duration.** The estimator interpolates both thresholds within the first completed excursion toward the final voltage. Returning below 10% before reaching 90% starts a new measurement. In the ringing regression, the result changes from 1.59 ns to 80 ps.
- **Timestep sizing across fixtures.** Use the shortest usable duration across all typical rising and falling waveform tables, regardless of fixture load. Even a third fixture can tighten the timestep when the converter fits switching weights from only the first two tables per direction. In #99, `prepareBlock` in `src/pipeline/signals.ts` sets the transient step to one twentieth of the fastest driver edge, one hundredth of the shortest bit period, or half the capture duration, whichever is smallest. `planRoutedBlock` in `src/pipeline/routed-admission.ts` also passes the fastest driver edge as `riseSeconds` for routed line cell sizing.
- **IBIS Ramp.** When the model has no usable typical waveform, the estimator uses the shortest usable typical rise or fall time from `IbisBuffer.ramp`. IBIS measures the 20–80% time into `R_load`. The constant-slope estimate for 10–90% scales that loaded time by 80% / 60% = 4/3. [Upstream ramp parsing](https://github.com/tscircuit/ibis-to-spice/pull/6)

The IBIS parser rejects waveform rows without a typical voltage, including when the model has a usable ramp. [Upstream waveform validation (#8)](https://github.com/tscircuit/ibis-to-spice/pull/8)

title: feat: inspect IBIS pin capabilities and references for channel endpoints
description: Resolves the buffer, pin capabilities and reference rails for selected channel endpoints. Stacked on 117. The inspection exports have no production callers in this layer. 99 uses them to prepare channels. Inspection resolves the selected pins rail overrides and vendor pin mappings through resolveIbisReferences and checks clamp voltages at the typical corner. It gets the typical voltages from resolveIbisReferenceVoltages, the same function the converter uses. It checks every selected pin binding for duplicates before skipping power, ground and unconnected pins. IBIS rail ports (7)(https:github.comtscircuitibis-to-spicepull7)  Shared reference voltages (8)(https:github.comtscircuitibis-to-spicepull8)
body:
Resolves the buffer, pin capabilities and reference rails for selected channel endpoints. Stacked on #117. The inspection exports have no production callers in this layer. #99 uses them to prepare channels.

Inspection resolves the selected pin’s rail overrides and vendor pin mappings through `resolveIbisReferences` and checks clamp voltages at the typical corner. It gets the typical voltages from `resolveIbisReferenceVoltages`, the same function the converter uses. It checks every selected pin binding for duplicates before skipping power, ground and unconnected pins. [IBIS rail ports (#7)](https://github.com/tscircuit/ibis-to-spice/pull/7) · [Shared reference voltages (#8)](https://github.com/tscircuit/ibis-to-spice/pull/8)

### New concepts

- **Pin binding.** A Circuit JSON source port identifies a physical IBIS pin. The pin names a buffer directly or lists choices through a model selector.
- **Pin capabilities.** The selected buffer type determines whether the pin can drive, receive or disable its output. Channel preparation uses these capabilities to validate endpoints.
- **IBIS references.** Reference roles identify the rails for drive, clamp and external connections. Channel preparation uses those ports and their typical voltages to bias the buffer.

title: feat: add isQuiet to board and the default capture duration to pipeline/timing
description: Adds isQuiet functionality to determine if a channel is quiet and sets a default capture duration for timing in the pipeline.
body:
Based on `main`.

Expose `isQuiet` and the PCB driver/receiver channel type from `board`. Add `defaultDurationSeconds` in `pipeline/timing` for block preparation in #99.

The constant-high waveform test runs in CI from #106 (ngspice installed in CI).

### New concepts

- **Unit interval.** One unit interval is one bit time. The default capture ends when the last channel completes one pattern at its own rate after its offset. Clock uses two unit intervals, a switching literal uses its bit count, and the default pseudo-random binary sequence (PRBS7) uses 127 unit intervals. PRBS15 and PRBS31 require an explicit duration.
- **Quiet channel.** A disabled driver or a constant bit pattern makes a channel quiet. A quiet channel contributes one unit interval from time zero regardless of its offset. #99's stimulus builder holds constant drivers at their initial level from t=0.

Downstream stages use the full waveform, and ngspice `.tran` starts from the DC operating point. Capturing one pattern avoids the long default recordings that prevented slower examples from finishing.

Explicit `duration` runs are unchanged.

AGENTS.md now uses mesh resolution as its named-constant example.

Rebased onto the Bun and Biome tooling PRs at the bottom of the stack.

Split the 13 signal and timing cases into one test per file and re-export the channel type from a single circuit-json import.

title: docs(agents): never rewrite a pushed PR's history
description: Adds a rule to AGENTS.md stating that pushed PR history should not be rewritten, emphasizing the importance of maintaining commit history for review purposes.
body:
Adds one rule to AGENTS.md under **Pull requests**: never rewrite a pushed PR's history.

PRs here are squash-merged, so the commits inside a PR are its review record. They show how each change, including an agent's, was made. Fixes go in as new commits. A stack is updated by merging the branch below into each PR above it, bottom to top, and by merging `main` after a lower PR is squash-merged. The one exception is a restructure the maintainer asks for explicitly, such as reordering, splitting or reviving PRs; that PR's description says the history was rewritten.

Based on `main`. Docs only.
